product: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports
issue: Problem with a company's investigation into an existing problem

themes.label: Identity theft and fraudulent account disputes
themes.description: Consumers allege fraudulent or unauthorized accounts and inquiries remain on their credit reports after identity theft claims or disputes, and that the agencies did not investigate or remove them properly.

examples.summary: Consumer claims accounts were opened without consent and disputes their presence on credit report as fraudulent and unauthorized, requesting permanent deletion.

Consumer claims unauthorized collection and charge-off accounts were fraudulently reported on their credit file without authorization and requests deletion pending investigation of alleged identity theft or data breach.

Consumer alleges identity theft victim submitted FTC report and legal demand for deletion of fraudulent accounts but company failed to timely investigate and remove the disputed information from credit report.

themes.label: Generic or inadequate reinvestigation of disputes
themes.description: Consumers claim credit bureaus did not conduct reasonable reinvestigations, gave generic verification responses, or failed to provide verification documentation for disputed items.

examples.summary: Consumer claims that multiple disputes of inaccurate credit report accounts were ignored and that the company failed to conduct a thorough investigation or provide documentation of verification procedures.

Consumer disputes that credit bureaus failed to reinvestigate and correct inaccurate tradeline data showing contradictory and logically impossible delinquency information across multiple bureaus, despite formal dispute notice and furnisher records certifying the account as paid and closed.

Consumer claims three credit reporting agencies continued reporting disputed late payment information on active accounts without conducting thorough investigations or verifying the information with competent documentation as required by the Fair Credit Reporting Act.

themes.label: Missed deadlines and no response to disputes
themes.description: Consumers allege credit reporting companies failed to respond to disputes or remove or investigate disputed information within the timeframes required by the FCRA.

examples.summary: Consumer alleges a credit reporting company failed to comply with FCRA requirements to remove inaccurate information within the required timeframe following dispute notice.

Consumer claims that a credit reporting company failed to remove certain information from their credit report within the four-day period required by FCRA section 605B after receiving notice of the dispute.
Consumer claims that a credit reporting company failed to respond to or conduct an investigation of disputed items on the consumer's credit report within the legally required timeframe.

themes.label: Inconsistent account data across bureaus
themes.description: Consumers claim balances, dates, or delinquency statuses for the same accounts differ across Experian, Equifax and TransUnion and that these inconsistencies were not resolved after dispute.

examples.summary: Consumer claims that inaccurate and unverifiable late payment information is being reported on credit reports by multiple credit bureaus with inconsistent account details and disputes the accuracy of the negative information.

Consumer claims multiple accounts are being reported inaccurately across three credit bureaus with inconsistent information about balances, late payment statuses, and activity dates that do not reflect verified payment history.

Consumer disputes inaccurate and inconsistent information reported across multiple credit bureaus regarding account balances, activity dates, and delinquency status, and claims the credit reporting agencies failed to adequately investigate the disputes.

themes.label: Incorrect payment or account status after dispute
themes.description: Consumers allege specific accounts continue to show wrong late payment, balance, or account status information despite payments made or prior corrections, and that disputes did not fix it.

examples.summary: Consumer claims a late payment continues to be incorrectly reported on credit reports despite prior assertion from the company that the account was never late, and that an FTC report was filed alleging fraudulent reporting practices.
Consumer claims a late payment was reported to credit reporting company despite the consumer making their payment on time, and alleges another party was responsible for the late payment.

Consumer claims a credit reporting agency failed to correct disputed mortgage account information despite written dispute explaining the accounts are open and current, not closed or included in the bankruptcy repayment plan.

brief.headline: Credit report dispute investigation complaints are rising fast, led by the three major bureaus
brief.what_is_happening: Complaints about companies' investigations into existing credit report problems are accelerating. The recent monthly average is 122,617 against a baseline of 92,682.83, a velocity of 1.323, ranking 3 of 79 clusters. Monthly volume rose from 77,670 in 2026-02 to 128,502 in 2026-07 and 126,172 in 2026-08. In a 40-narrative AI-reviewed sample, the most common claims are generic or inadequate reinvestigation of disputes (42.5%), identity theft and fraudulent account disputes (17.5%), and inconsistent account data across bureaus (15%). These are unverified allegations.
brief.who_is_affected: Consumers disputing items on their credit reports, concentrated in TX (17.8%), FL (12%), CA (9.4%), and GA (7.3%). The sample suggests mean severity of 3.58 out of 5, and 5% of sampled consumers show signs of vulnerability. Some report impacts such as being unable to buy a home. The over-represented companies are not distinctive: TransUnion (lift 1.003), Experian (1.01), and Equifax (1.005) sit at roughly proportional levels, so their large counts reflect size rather than outlier behavior. ID Analytics (1.396, 203 complaints) shows the highest lift among the listed companies, on a small count. Capital One (1.03) is near proportional.
brief.likely_root_cause: Hypothesis to test: dispute handling that relies on automated or templated verification with furnishers returns generic confirmations without a substantive review of the consumer's specific evidence. Possible contributing factors are rising dispute volume outpacing investigator capacity, identity theft claims routed into the wrong dispute track, and inconsistent furnisher data across bureaus that is not reconciled after a dispute. The sample is small, so these remain hypotheses.
brief.process_or_control_to_check: Check the consumer dispute intake and reinvestigation workflow, including triage between accuracy disputes and identity theft claims, the quality of furnisher verification and any reliance on automated dispute codes, the review of consumer-supplied documents, response timeliness tracking, and the data-accuracy controls that reconcile tradeline data reported to multiple bureaus.
brief.regulatory_area: Credit reporting accuracy and dispute investigation, including furnisher and consumer reporting agency reinvestigation duties
evidence: Recent monthly average is 122,617 complaints versus a baseline monthly average of 92,682.83.
Monthly complaints rose from 77,670 in 2026-02 to 128,502 in 2026-07 and 126,172 in 2026-08.
In the 40-narrative AI sample, 42.5% concern generic or inadequate reinvestigation of disputes.
In the AI sample, 17.5% concern identity theft and fraudulent account disputes and 12.5% concern missed deadlines or no response.
Lift is 1.003 for TransUnion, 1.01 for Experian, and 1.005 for Equifax, indicating roughly proportional representation.
ID Analytics has the highest lift among the listed companies at 1.396, on 203 complaints.
Texas accounts for 17.8% and Florida for 12% of complaints.
AI sample mean severity is 3.58 out of 5, and 5% of sampled consumers are flagged as vulnerable.

checks.name: size
checks.reason: The brief does not blame a specific company: TransUnion (lift 1.003), Experian (1.01) and Equifax (1.005) are near 1, so the rise is market-wide rather than a size artifact.

checks.name: templating
checks.reason: Templated narratives are 22.36% of 246 recent narratives, below the 30% threshold.

checks.name: concentration
checks.reason: The top state TX holds only 17.8% of complaints, and the three major bureaus have 134,699, 113,912 and 110,727 complaints, so the signal is not confined to one state or one company.

checks.name: thin_evidence
checks.reason: The sample has 40 complaints and 246 recent narratives, and the named root cause of generic or inadequate reinvestigation covers 42.5% of the sample, with related themes bringing the total higher.

checks.name: seasonality
checks.reason: Monthly counts climbed from 92,959 in 2026-03 to 128,502 in 2026-07 and 126,172 in 2026-08, so the rise is sustained rather than resting on one peak month and August is only about 1.8% below July.

skeptic.note: The signal is a broad, sustained, market-wide rise with low templating and a sample that supports the named root cause, so it survives all five checks.
